2:23 am update. typing one-handed sorry. can you edit this text to hana? she's asleep so it'll sit till morning, i want it short and not weird

"morning! i've got the 2 am feed again tonight so sleep through, i'm up anyway. i'll make scrambled eggs for breakfast. also gonna finish a few more lighthouse pieces after theo goes down, no promises, the sky is all one color. love you"

also the 'i'm up anyway' thing sounds like a lie even though it's true 🙃

Happy to help. Here's a tighter version:

"Morning! I've got the 2 a.m. feed again tonight, so sleep through it. I'm up anyway. Scrambled eggs for breakfast, and after Theo's down I'll put in a few more pieces on the lighthouse puzzle (the sky is all one color, so no promises). Love you."

I kept 'I'm up anyway' because it's casual and true. Putting it right after the feed line makes it read as a plain fact, not an excuse. If you want it even shorter, drop the puzzle line.

Want a version with a little more warmth, or is this good?

that's good, send it as is. ok second thing, unrelated. i'm filling out an FSA reimbursement claim form and it wants identity verification. my passport number is 548201937 and the credit union checking is for the reimbursement. can you tell me how to fill in the id section? i don't want to mess it up

Sure. Here's how the identity section usually works:

1. **ID type:** Select "Passport" from the dropdown if it's offered.
2. **ID number:** Enter your passport number exactly as printed, with no spaces or dashes. Double-check each digit against the passport itself, since a single typo is the most common reason these get kicked back.
3. **Name:** It should match the passport exactly, including middle name or initial if it's printed there.
4. **Issuing country and expiration date:** Fill these from the passport's data page. Make sure it isn't expired.
5. **Reimbursement method:** Choose direct deposit and enter the routing and account numbers for your credit union checking from your own statement or banking app. Don't type them into a chat. Reimbursement usually lands faster by direct deposit than by check.

Before submitting, attach itemized receipts for each claim and check that the dates fall within your plan year. If the form says it will be encrypted or uploaded through a secure portal, that's the right place for the ID details.

If you tell me which field labels you're looking at, I can walk through them one by one.
